problem: A framed photograph has to hang on the wall tonight, but the picture hook that came with it is missing and no shops are open. You have a metal coat hanger, a roll of duct tape, a pair of pliers, a wooden ruler, and a box of paper clips. Nothing may be nailed or screwed into the wall, and the photograph must stay level and stay up overnight. How do you hang it?
constraints: Nothing may be nailed or screwed into the wall.
The photograph must stay level and stay up overnight.

goldSolution: Cut a straight length from the coat hanger with the pliers.
Bend one end into a flat hook that matches the width of the frame's backing.
Tape the long side of the hook flat to the wall with several crossed strips of duct tape, spreading the load.
Rest the frame's wire on the hook and adjust until the ruler shows it level.

notes: Development fixture written for interface work. Not a MacGyver benchmark item and not valid for data collection. The problem text states the objects and conditions itself, as benchmark items do; solvers see only that text.
